pre.speaker: narrator
pre.text: Bowang, in the ninth year after Xiapi. Xiahou Dun is coming south with Cao Cao's vanguard, and Liu Bei has a new adviser who has never led a company in his life.

pre.speaker: zhang-fei
pre.text: So the scholar gets the seals, and I go where he points. Fine. Once. If it goes wrong I will say what I think of it, loudly.

pre.speaker: zhuge-liang
pre.text: I expect nothing less, General Zhang. Listen. Bowang is a cleft of reeds between two wooded slopes, narrowing to a neck before our camp. General Guan will take the western slope, General Zhang the eastern one.

pre.speaker: zhao-yun
pre.text: And I am the bait. I have been called worse. Where do I stand?

pre.speaker: zhuge-liang
pre.text: In the neck, where the reeds are thickest, and you will let Xiahou Dun think you are afraid. He will come down the valley after you. He is a man who follows what he is angry at.

pre.speaker: guan-yu
pre.text: Reeds burn. But not before the wind is right, or we cook our own.

pre.speaker: zhuge-liang
pre.text: At dusk of the fourth day the wind turns off the pass and runs south along the valley. Until then, patience. After it, the reeds are my business.

post.speaker: narrator
post.text: The reeds burned all night, and the valley of Bowang smelled of smoke for a week. Xiahou Dun rode north with a third of the men he brought.

post.speaker: zhang-fei
post.text: The wind was where he said it would be. I would like it noted that I was not worried. Not very.

post.speaker: guan-yu
post.text: It is noted. He has earned the seals, brother.

post.speaker: liu-bei
post.text: Master Zhuge, you have given us a victory when I had nothing to give you but a hut's welcome. I do not forget it.

post.speaker: zhuge-liang
post.text: It was a small valley and a small army, my lord. Cao Cao will not take it quietly. The first order is always the easy one.
